hero.title: Bodhisamadhi Center
hero.mission: A Gelug Tibetan Buddhist dharma center in Toronto — devoted to meditation, the purification of mind, and the cultivation of wisdom and compassion for all sentient beings. Founded 2016 by Venerable Geshe Sonam Topgyal of Sera Mey Monastery.

features.heading: Practice, Learn & Connect
features.intro: Bodhisamadhi Center offers a full path of Gelug practice — from weekly pujas and monthly teachings to an online library, event registration, and personal spiritual guidance.
features.dharmaIntro_p: An accessible introduction to Buddhist philosophy and the Gelug tradition — ideal for newcomers beginning their path.
features.scriptureStudy_p: In-depth study of canonical texts — Lamrim, Madhyamaka, Vinaya and tantra — guided by Geshe-la in three languages.
features.meditation_p: Guided meditation instruction in calm-abiding and insight — from foundational breathing to advanced Gelug visualization practices.
features.blessings_p: Ritual blessings and prayers for health, protection, long life and auspiciousness — led by Geshe-la for individuals and families.
features.butterLamp_p: Offer butter lamps on behalf of loved ones — for merit accumulation, healing, or in memory of the deceased. Requests fulfilled at each puja.
features.dedication_p: Puja dedication and merit transference for the living and the deceased — including Amitabha services conducted with care and privacy.
features.counseling_p: One-on-one spiritual counseling rooted in Dharma wisdom — for grief, anxiety, life transitions, or deepening one's practice.
features.guidance_p: End-of-life spiritual support — prayers and compassionate guidance for the dying and their families, in full confidence.
features.assembly_p: Regular community practice sessions and group study for lay practitioners — in person and online, fostering Dharma friendship and shared aspiration.
features.guruPuja_p: Guru Puja (Tib. Lama Chöpa) is one of the most important tantric practices in the Gelug tradition, typically held on the 10th and 25th of the Tibetan lunar month. Practitioners gather to make feast offerings, recite prayers to the lineage masters, and deepen their connection to the guru — the very root of the Vajrayāna path. Tsog offerings are shared communally as blessed substances, and the merit generated benefits all beings. Open to those with Vajrayāna commitment.
features.lungta_p: Lungta, or Wind Horse prayer flags, are a cherished Tibetan tradition for calling forth good fortune, health, and spiritual merit. Printed with sacred mantras, prayers, and the image of the Wind Horse, they are raised at auspicious times — such as Losar (Tibetan New Year) or significant life events — so that each breath of wind carries blessings to all beings in the ten directions. The center organises communal flag-raising ceremonies where participants offer prayers together and dedicate the merit for the benefit of all sentient beings.
features.lifeRelease_p: Life Release (Tib. Tse Tar) is one of the most powerful practices for accumulating merit, purifying negative karma, and extending life. By purchasing animals destined for slaughter and freeing them — fish, birds, or other creatures — practitioners directly enact the Buddha's teaching on compassion and the preciousness of life. Mantras and prayers are recited over the animals before release, planting seeds of liberation in their minds. The center organises group Tse Tar activities throughout the year, welcoming all who wish to participate.

howItWorks.heading: How to Participate
howItWorks.intro: Whether you are new to Tibetan Buddhism or a long-time practitioner, there is a place for you here — in Toronto or online.
howItWorks.discover_p: Browse our teachings, masters and schedule. Watch recorded Dharma talks and read about the Gelug lineage and our six aspirations.
howItWorks.attend_p: Visit the center for weekly pujas and monthly teachings — call ahead so we can welcome you. Join livestreams when available.
howItWorks.register_p: Create an account to register for events, access the full library, request pujas, and receive teachings by email.
howItWorks.support_p: Sustain the Dharma through offerings, puja sponsorship, volunteering (translation, events), or recurring monthly giving.

testimonials.heading: What Practitioners Say
testimonials.q1: "Geshe-la's teaching style is remarkably clear — he explains tantra and Madhyamaka in a way that is accessible whether you follow in Chinese, Tibetan or English. The weekly Yamantaka puja has become the anchor of my practice."
testimonials.q2: "When my mother passed away, the center supported our family with such care and respect. Geshe-la's guidance through that difficult period gave our entire family tremendous peace of mind."
testimonials.q3: "I came to Bodhisamadhi Center with no background in Tibetan Buddhism. Within a year I had received my first empowerment, completed a short retreat, and felt real transformation in how I respond to stress and difficulty."

events.heading: Schedule & Events
events.intro: The schedule below reflects the center's regular programming.
events.yamantaka_p: Weekly sadhana guided by Geshe-la. Open to all — beginners and experienced practitioners alike. Call for time.
events.vajrayogini_p: Bi-weekly sadhana with confession and merit accumulation (tsog). Call for exact dates.
events.teaching_p: Monthly Dharma talk by Geshe-la — Lamrim, Madhyamaka, tantra. Trilingual (Tibetan / Chinese / English).
events.empowerment_p: Annual empowerment and homa for Gelug deities. Registration required — check Facebook or call for dates.
events.request_p: Medicine Buddha, Tara, Dzambhala and Amitabha puja. Handled with full privacy. Call or email to request.

library.heading: Listen, Watch & Read
library.intro: A growing library of recorded teachings, ritual chants and downloadable practice texts. Browse the newest additions below.

give.heading: Offer Your Support
give.intro: Bodhisamadhi Center is a registered Canadian charity (No. 713674927RT0001). Every offering sustains daily pujas, the shrine, and the translation mission. Tax receipts issued for eligible donations.
give.oneTime_p: Support daily pujas, butter lamps and shrine upkeep. Any amount is welcome.
give.monthly_p: Set up a recurring monthly gift to provide stable support. Annual Canadian tax receipts sent automatically.
give.sponsor_p: Dedicate a puja — Medicine Buddha, Tara, Dzambhala, or Amitabha — for health, protection, prosperity, or the peace of the departed.
give.volunteer_p: Offer your time and skills — translation, event logistics, photography, web support. Contact us to get involved.

cta.heading: Come As You Are
cta.intro: Bodhisamadhi Center welcomes anyone who seeks peace of mind, a deeper understanding of Tibetan Buddhist philosophy, or a trilingual community of practice in Toronto. No prior knowledge of Buddhism is required.
cta.note: Please call before your first visit: {phone} · Open daily 6:00–11:00 am
